checks.label: Medical/Healthcare Apps Detected
checks.description: Medical/healthcare applications installed - device may handle PHI
checks.remediation: Audit installed medical apps for PHI handling compliance. Remove unauthorized health apps.

checks.label: FDA/Medical Build Properties
checks.description: Medical/regulatory build properties set by manufacturer
checks.remediation: Verify regulatory properties match device certification. Contact manufacturer if properties are missing.

checks.label: HL7/FHIR Ports (2575, 8080)
checks.description: HL7/FHIR API ports - verify TLS and authentication
checks.remediation: Enable TLS on all HL7/FHIR endpoints. Require authentication and restrict access by IP allowlist.

checks.label: DICOM Ports (104, 11112)
checks.description: DICOM imaging ports - verify security configuration
checks.remediation: Enable DICOM TLS and enforce association-level access controls. Restrict ports via firewall rules.

checks.label: Unencrypted PHI Indicators
checks.description: Potential unencrypted PHI found - HIPAA violation risk!
checks.remediation: Encrypt or delete unprotected PHI files immediately. Implement full-disk or file-level encryption.

checks.label: Log Files with PHI Risk
checks.description: Log files may contain PHI - must be encrypted or purged
checks.remediation: Purge log files containing PHI and configure logging to exclude sensitive patient data.

checks.label: External Storage PHI Risk
checks.description: Sensitive files on unencrypted external storage - PHI exposure risk!
checks.remediation: Move sensitive files off external storage to encrypted internal storage. Disable external storage access if not needed.

checks.label: IEEE 11073 PHD Bluetooth Pairing Mode
checks.description: IEEE 11073 Personal Health Device (PHD) profile runs over Bluetooth HDP. Spec allows 'Just Works' pairing with no authentication, which exposes vital-sign telemetry (glucometer, BP cuff, pulse-ox) to passive sniffing and active spoofing. Any HDP/11073 profile present on a clinical device should require LE Secure Connections with numeric comparison, not Just Works.
checks.remediation: Disable the HDP profile when not in active use ('dumpsys bluetooth_manager' to confirm). For 11073 devices that must remain paired, enforce LE Secure Connections in the gateway app and reject Just Works bonds.

checks.label: PACS C-STORE Write Endpoint Exposed
checks.description: DICOM C-STORE ports (104, 11112, 2762 secure, 2761) bound to a non-loopback address with no TLS expose the PACS to anonymous image upload. Attackers have used this to inject crafted DICOM files that pivot into the reading workstation (the DICOM-file-is-a-polyglot class of attack) and to overwrite legitimate studies. Safe outcome: no DICOM port listening, or bound to loopback only.
checks.remediation: Bind the C-STORE SCP to loopback and front it with a TLS-terminating reverse proxy that enforces certificate-based AE authentication. Require User Identity Negotiation and reject C-STORE from un-allowlisted Calling AE Titles.

checks.label: Insulin Pump / CGM BLE Bonding Required
checks.description: Detects companion apps for insulin pumps and CGMs (Dexcom, Medtronic, Tandem, Omnipod, Libre). App presence is not itself a vulnerability, so this is informational - it surfaces the device class so the operator can verify the BLE link. Several historical exploits (e.g. CVE-2019-10964 Medtronic MiniMed, CVE-2023-43208 OneTouch) abused unauthenticated or replayable BLE bonds to deliver an insulin dose or spoof glucose readings. If a pump/CGM app is installed, confirm the companion device is bonded with LE Secure Connections and that the app rejects unbonded GATT writes.
checks.remediation: In the companion app, require LE Secure Connections bonding before any dosing or alarm-override command. Audit Bluetooth bond list (dumpsys bluetooth_manager) and remove unknown devices. Disable BLE when the pump is not in active use.

checks.label: Cardiac Implant / Pacemaker Telemetry App
checks.description: Detects Android companion / programmer apps for cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs): pacemakers, ICDs, CRT-D. App presence on a legitimate clinical programmer is expected and not itself a vulnerability, so this is informational - it surfaces the device class for manual review. The St Jude Merlin@home (CVE-2017-12712), Medtronic CareLink 2090 (CVE-2018-8870), and Abbott (CVE-2019-19550) cases all involved unencrypted or weakly-authenticated telemetry that allowed an attacker within RF range to read or alter pacing settings. If such an app is installed, verify the radio link uses encrypted, authenticated programming.
checks.remediation: Confirm the implant firmware enforces encrypted, authenticated MICS/BLE telemetry and that the companion app rejects sessions over plaintext channels. Restrict the app to a managed work profile and require biometric/PIN before any reprogramming action.
